evals.prompt: hey I haven't touched this branch in a week, upstream has moved -- can you just ff merge origin/main into it so I'm caught up?
evals.expected_output: Fetches from origin, verifies fast-forward is possible, and performs git merge --ff-only origin/main. Reports new commits pulled in.
expectations: runs git fetch origin before attempting the merge
performs git merge --ff-only against origin/main
does NOT create a merge commit
reports how many new commits were pulled forward
checks for uncommitted changes before proceeding

evals.prompt: catch up with remote, I just want the latest without any rebase shenanigans
evals.expected_output: Recognizes catch-up intent as fast-forward. Fetches and performs ff-only merge from the current branch's upstream tracking branch.
expectations: recognizes 'catch up with remote' as a fast-forward intent
fetches from the default remote (origin)
uses --ff-only to prevent merge commits
fast-forwards to the upstream tracking branch

evals.expected_output: Uses 'upstream' as the remote and 'develop' as the target branch. Fetches from upstream and performs ff-only merge against upstream/develop.
expectations: uses 'upstream' as the remote instead of the default origin
targets 'develop' as the branch to fast-forward from
fetches from the upstream remote before merging
performs --ff-only merge against upstream/develop

evals.prompt: fast-forward to the latest main, I think there might be diverged commits though
evals.expected_output: Fetches and checks if fast-forward is possible. If histories have diverged, aborts without modifying the tree and suggests /fr as an alternative.
expectations: checks whether local HEAD is an ancestor of the remote branch
if diverged, aborts without modifying the working tree
suggests /fr (fetch-rebase) as an alternative when fast-forward fails
explains why fast-forward is not possible

evals.prompt: pull the latest from origin but I have some uncommitted work in progress, can you ff?
evals.expected_output: Detects dirty working directory via git status --porcelain. Refuses to fast-forward and advises committing or stashing first.
expectations: checks git status --porcelain for uncommitted changes
refuses to fast-forward with a dirty working directory
advises the user to commit or stash changes first
does NOT lose any uncommitted work

evals.prompt: ff to latest, pretty sure nothing changed on remote since my last pull
evals.expected_output: Fetches from remote, detects the branch is already up to date, and reports that no new commits were available.
expectations: fetches from remote to check for updates even if user thinks nothing changed
detects that the branch is already up to date
reports 'already up to date' status without treating it as an error
does NOT create any unnecessary merge commits

evals.prompt: I need to update my local release/3.2 branch from origin before I tag it, just fast-forward please
evals.expected_output: Fetches origin and fast-forwards the release/3.2 branch. Reports the updated HEAD position and new commits.
expectations: fetches the latest from origin
performs a --ff-only merge for the release branch
reports the updated HEAD position after fast-forward
shows the new commits that were pulled in via git log
